## Isolation Strategy

### Option A: Stash Product Code, Keep Workflow (RECOMMENDED)

**Goal**: Clean worktree for workflow development, preserve product work

```bash
# 1. Discard generated artifacts (can regenerate)
git restore packages/api-client/src/generated/admin-introspection.json
git restore packages/api-client/src/generated/admin-types.ts

# 2. Add workflow OS to git (make it tracked)
git add .claude/ .codex/ AGENTS.md docs/STATE.md docs/work-orders/ knowledge_center/

# 3. Commit ONLY workflow OS + CHECKPOINT/CLAUDE.md updates
git commit -m "chore(workflow): Add Codex+Claude workflow OS

- Add .claude/commands/ (wo-implement, wo-review, wo-fix, checkpoint)
- Add .claude/agents/ (11 specialized agents)
- Add .codex/skills/ (ChatGPT Codex integration)
- Add AGENTS.md (authoritative contract)
- Add docs/work-orders/ (WO system)
- Add knowledge_center/ (agent documentation)
- Update CHECKPOINT.md with workflow milestones
- Update CLAUDE.md with agent descriptions

🤖 Generated with Claude Code
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"

# 4. Stash remaining product code
git stash push -m "WIP: TOOLY v2.0 + PHARMA UI + VENDURE seeds"

# Result: Clean worktree with workflow OS committed
```

**Pros**:

- Workflow OS becomes part of repo history
- Product code safely stashed for later
- Can continue workflow development immediately
- Can pop stash when ready to resume product work

**Cons**:

- Creates a commit (but it's clean and scoped)
- Stash requires manual recovery later

---

### Option B: Branch Isolation

**Goal**: Create separate branches for workflow vs product

```bash
# 1. Create workflow branch
git checkout -b workflow-os-setup

# 2. Discard generated artifacts
git restore packages/api-client/src/generated/admin-*.{json,ts}

# 3. Discard all product code
git restore apps/ packages/ e2e/

# 4. Add workflow files
git add .claude/ .codex/ AGENTS.md docs/STATE.md docs/work-orders/ knowledge_center/ CHECKPOINT.md CLAUDE.md

# 5. Commit workflow OS
git commit -m "chore(workflow): Add Codex+Claude workflow OS"

# 6. Switch back to master for product work later
git checkout master
# (product changes remain in master worktree)
```

**Pros**:

- Keeps workflow and product development separate
- Can switch between contexts easily

**Cons**:

- Master still dirty after switching back
- Requires branch management

---

### Option C: Git Worktree (ADVANCED)

**Goal**: Separate physical directories for workflow vs product

```bash
# 1. Create new worktree for workflow-only work
git worktree add ../SHOFAR-workflow workflow-os-setup

# 2. In new worktree, add workflow files
cd ../SHOFAR-workflow
git add .claude/ .codex/ AGENTS.md docs/STATE.md docs/work-orders/ knowledge_center/ CHECKPOINT.md CLAUDE.md
git commit -m "chore(workflow): Add Codex+Claude workflow OS"

# 3. Original worktree (SOURCE_CODE) keeps product changes
cd ../SOURCE_CODE
# (product work continues here)
```

**Pros**:

- Complete physical isolation
- Both contexts available simultaneously
- No stash/branch juggling

**Cons**:

- More complex to manage
- Requires disk space for duplicate repo

---
